prompt: CHALLENGE: Why does ethanol boil (78 °C) more than 100 °C higher than ethane (−89 °C), despite similar molecular weights?

options.label: Hydrogen bonding between OH groups creates a network that requires energy to break.
Only polarity matters, not H-bonding specifically.

explanation: Each OH can act as both an H-bond donor and acceptor, so ethanol molecules form 2D networks. Breaking those H-bonds (~5 kcal/mol each) requires significant energy — hence the ~170 K boiling point difference vs ethane which has only London forces.
